title: OCR bounding-box arithmetic can overflow

attack_path_facts.title: OCR bounding-box arithmetic can overflow
attack_steps: The operator invokes an approved OCR operation.
The remote OCR service returns the accepted array bounding-box form with extreme signed 64-bit coordinates.
KCS computes x+w or y+h without checked arithmetic or geometry validation.
A debug build panics and aborts the operation, while a release build can wrap the values and persist invalid extracted-image metadata.
assumptions: Online OCR is enabled and the remote response actor can choose bounding-box coordinates.
The response uses the array form that reaches the unchecked additions.
attack_path_facts.context: The remote response is an in-scope untrusted source. The missing arithmetic check lets that source affect process availability or derived metadata beyond a normal rejected OCR response, but it does not bypass authorization.
attack_path_facts.exposure: Outbound OCR client workflow controlled by the configured remote service; no inbound KCS listener exists.
attack_path_facts.identity: The KCS user performs an approved OCR call; the remote service controls the response coordinates but gains no KCS credential or filesystem identity.
preconditions: An approved OCR request must reach the configured service.
The response must include the accepted array bounding-box representation.
Coordinates must overflow signed 64-bit addition or otherwise form unreasonable geometry.
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes: the in-scope remote response actor directly controls x, y, width, and height
attack_path_facts.category: remote-response integer overflow causing process availability or metadata-integrity failure
mitigations: Only the accepted array form reaches the addition; other forms are unaffected.
Adapter approval is required before the request.
The failure is confined to OCR processing and does not authorize a different destination or read.
attack_path_facts.auth_scope: remote response to a previously approved OCR call
attack_path_facts.impact_surface: OCR runtime availability and extracted-image metadata integrity
attack_path_facts.target_reach: the active OCR operation and its process/batch; no cross-scope persistence was shown
secrets_references: The configured OCR credential is used for the approved request, with no demonstrated disclosure or forwarding.
counterevidence: The remote service already can fail its own OCR response, and this issue adds no authorization bypass.
Only one response representation reaches the overflow.
The report shows panic or invalid coordinates, not durable cross-scope corruption.
blindspots: The final receipt does not demonstrate end-to-end release-build persistence or downstream use of wrapped coordinates.
Batch-wide recovery effects after a panic are not measured.
attack_path_facts.rationale: The remote response actor directly controls the unchecked operands during an ordinary approved call. The resulting availability/metadata harm is bounded to OCR and carries no auth bypass, so impact is Medium; remote direct control makes likelihood High, mapping to Medium/P2.
